'''John Edward McCarthy''' (born 20 January 1964) is a mathematician. He is currently the [[Spencer Truman Olin|Spencer T. Olin]] Professor of Arts and Sciences, and former chair of the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.wustl.edu/wp/mccarthy/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/cv-jm_Feb2025.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|date=February 2025|access-date=2025-05-23}}</ref> He works in [[operator theory]]<ref name=beauty/> and [[complex analysis|several complex variables]], and applications of [[mathematics]] to other areas.

==Early life, education, and career==
McCarthy is a native of Ireland, and received a B.A. from [[Trinity College Dublin]], in 1983.<ref name=beauty>{{Cite web |last=Fitzpatrick |first=Tony |date=January 23, 2004 |title=The beauty of pure mathematics: The applicability of the field isn't the only thing that motivates John E. McCarthy|work=Newsroom|publisher=Washington University in St. Louis|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2004/01/the-beauty-of-pure-mathematics/ |access-date=2025-05-23 }}</ref> He completed a Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1989. His Ph.D. Advisor was [[Donald Sarason]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|32503}}</ref>

He originally intended to return to Ireland after his doctorate, but the Irish universities were subject to a hiring freeze at the time. Instead, after postdoctoral research at [[Indiana University Bloomington]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Two Indianapolis residents named Kelley Scholar at IU |url=https://newsinfo.iu.edu/news/page/normal/3745.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604173139/https://newsinfo.iu.edu/news/page/normal/3745.html |archive-date=June 4, 2024 |access-date= |website=newsinfo.iu.edu}}</ref> he joined Washington University in St. Louis in 1991, and became a US citizen in 1996.<ref name=beauty/> He has been a full professor since 1999, and Spencer T. Olin Professor of [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]] since 2011. He chaired the Department of Mathematics and Statistics from 2016 to 2021.<ref name=cv/>

==Recognition==
McCarthy was one of two 2016 recipients of the [[Gilbert de Beauregard Robinson]] Award of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/Prizes/info/gbr.html|title=G. de B. Robinson Award|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-05-23}}</ref> He was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-05-23}}</ref>

==Books==
McCarthy's books include:
*''Holomorphic Spaces'' (edited with [[Sheldon Axler]] and [[Donald Sarason]]), [[Cambridge University Press]], 1998.
* ''Pick Interpolation and Hilbert function spaces'' (with [[Jim Agler]]), [[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]], vol. 44, [[American Mathematical Society]], 2002.<ref>Reviews of ''Pick Interpolation and Hilbert function spaces'': [[Donald Sarason]], {{MR|1882259}}; Vladimir V.Peller, {{zbl| 1010.47001}}</ref>
* ''Transition to Higher Mathematics: Structure and Proof'' (with Bob A. Dumas), 1st ed., [[McGraw Hill]], 2006; 2nd. ed., Washington University Open Scholarship, 2015.
* ''Operator Analysis: Hilbert space methods in complex analysis'' (with Jim Agler and [[Nicholas Young (mathematician)|Nicholas Young]]), Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics, vol. 219, [[Cambridge University Press]], 2020.<ref>Reviews of ''Operator Analysis'': [[Adhemar Bultheel]], {{MR|4411370}}; Dan Timotin, {{zbl|1498.47001}}</ref>
